hoobuy-size-chart-workflow-measurements-.title: HooBuy Size Chart Guide 2026: Spreadsheet Workflow
hoobuy-size-chart-workflow-measurements-.description: Use a HooBuy size chart without guessing: record exact variants, measurement endpoints, units, tolerances and reference-garment comparisons.
hoobuy-size-chart-workflow-measurements-.body:
A HooBuy size chart is useful only when its numbers describe the same measurement you can reproduce. Choosing by a familiar letter, height range or automatic conversion can create false confidence because two sellers may use the same label for different finished dimensions.

The spreadsheet method below preserves the original chart, defines each endpoint and compares it with a garment or foot measurement taken the same way. It also keeps uncertainty visible. The aim is not to predict a perfect fit; it is to make a better documented choice and know which later warehouse evidence could reveal a mismatch.

Verify the exact listing and selected variant first

Open the final destination page and save its marketplace, item identifier, seller identity, final URL and verification date. Select the intended color, version and other options before copying the size chart. Some pages reuse images or display information that may not apply equally to every option.

If the destination, seller or item cannot be reproduced, pause the sizing decision and use the product-link verification workflow. Accurate measurements attached to the wrong listing remain wrong evidence.

Preserve the original chart before normalizing it

Record every source size label, value, unit, measurement name, tolerance statement and explanatory note exactly as displayed. Keep the observation date. If you make a private reference image where permitted, also transcribe the important values into structured cells so they can be filtered and compared.

Add normalized columns only beside the source data. A conversion formula should never overwrite the original number. Round consistently and avoid manufacturing precision; a whole-centimeter chart does not become more accurate when converted to two decimal places.

Source fieldContext to keepDo not assume
ChestFlat width or circumferenceThat every seller uses the same method
LengthStarting and ending landmarkThat front and back lengths match
SleeveShoulder seam or center-back pathThat raglan and set-in sleeves compare directly
WaistBody or finished garment basisThat stretch is already included
Foot lengthFoot, insole, interior or outsoleThat one number represents all four

Classify every value by measurement type

Use explicit types: body measurement, finished-garment measurement, flat measurement, circumference, foot measurement, insole length, interior length or outsole length. Values with different types should not be compared directly even when their units match.

If the chart simply says “chest” or “length” without a diagram or method, mark the endpoint as not stated. Do not resolve ambiguity by choosing the interpretation that best supports the desired size. Write one clear blocking question instead.

Core rule: same label plus same unit does not mean same measurement. Compare only values with matching object, endpoints, state and method.

Choose a reference item that already fits

For clothing, select a garment of similar type and intended fit. Lay it on a flat surface without stretching it. Measure the endpoints used by the seller chart, repeat important values and record the date, tool and reference item.

For footwear, measure the intended foot using a consistent method and time, then compare only with a chart that clearly states a compatible basis. A labeled shoe size or a generic country conversion should remain a separate clue rather than replacing the listing-specific evidence.

Account for construction and intended fit

A chest measurement alone cannot describe shoulder width, armhole shape, fabric behavior or preferred ease. Create fields for the intended fit—close, regular or oversized—and for construction details that materially affect the decision. Keep these as decision inputs, not universal rules.

Compare several dimensions when available. A size may appear suitable at the chest but fail on body length or sleeve path. The spreadsheet should flag the conflicting dimension rather than averaging everything into one “good” result.

Handle stretch and tolerance cautiously

If a listing states a measurement tolerance, preserve the exact wording and unit. Do not apply a tolerance from one seller to another. If stretch is claimed, record where the claim appears, but do not invent a stretch percentage or assume that elasticity produces a comfortable fit.

Create low and high comparison bounds only when the source supports them. When no tolerance is provided, label the value as a point observation with unknown production variation. Visible uncertainty is more honest and useful than a made-up safety margin.

Keep size recommendations separate from measurements

Seller recommendations based on height, weight or a message belong in attributed fields with the date and exact selected variant. They can be considered, but they should not overwrite the chart or the reference-item comparison.

If a recommendation conflicts with reproducible garment measurements, expose the conflict and pause. The next useful step is clarification, not silently selecting whichever answer feels safer. Record who supplied the recommendation and what information they used.

Build a simple comparison calculation

For each matching dimension, calculate candidate measurement minus reference measurement. Keep the result in the same unit and label its direction. A positive value means the candidate is larger on that measured path; it does not automatically mean the fit is better.

Add a decision band based on the intended fit and the user’s own acceptable range. This is a personal preference field, not a platform standard. If only one important dimension matches while another is absent, the status should remain incomplete.

Plan measurement QC without overclaiming

Before ordering, identify which selected-size label and finished-product measurements need confirmation after warehouse arrival. State the exact endpoints and whether the garment should be laid flat. Use statuses such as pending, readable, measured, method unclear, mismatch or not shown.

A tag photo can confirm a visible label but not the true garment dimensions or fit. A tape photo can show a measured path only if both endpoints and the reading are clear. Neither proves comfort, drape after wear or production consistency beyond the specific item.

Worked example: two hoodies labeled large

Candidate A lists a flat chest width and back length with a diagram. Candidate B uses the same “L” label but provides only a body-weight suggestion. The reference hoodie has measurements taken with endpoints matching Candidate A.

A can be compared dimension by dimension and moved forward if the differences meet the intended fit. B remains unresolved because its recommendation uses a different evidence type. Calling both products the same size would hide the most important difference in the record.

Use stop conditions instead of optimistic guesses

  • The chart cannot be tied to the exact listing or selected variant.
  • Measurement type or endpoints are not stated for a critical dimension.
  • Units are missing or a translation is ambiguous.
  • The candidate and reference measurements use incompatible methods.
  • An important dimension conflicts with the intended fit.
  • A recommendation conflicts with the reproducible chart.
  • The selected size is unavailable or changes another product option.
  • The after-sale assumption has not been checked in the live account.

Minimum size-chart spreadsheet fields

  1. Stable candidate ID and verified listing identity.
  2. Exact selected option labels and observation date.
  3. Original chart values, units and notes.
  4. Measurement type and defined endpoints.
  5. Normalized values in separate calculated columns.
  6. Reference item and matching measurement method.
  7. Intended fit and acceptable comparison range.
  8. Seller recommendation stored as attributed evidence.
  9. Conflicts, unknowns and blocking questions.
  10. Planned warehouse checks and final decision reason.

Freeze the decision, then append later evidence

Before ordering, save the row version that informed the choice. After warehouse arrival, append the received label and measurement evidence without replacing the source chart. A mismatch should remain visible so the buyer can inspect current options using the correct record.

The wider HooBuy spreadsheet guide explains how to maintain status and verification dates. Used together, these fields turn a size chart from a persuasive image into an auditable comparison: exact source, matched method, visible uncertainty and a clear next action.

hoobuy-holiday-shopping-timeline-spreads.title: HooBuy Holiday Shopping Timeline 2026: Spreadsheet Plan
hoobuy-holiday-shopping-timeline-spreads.description: Build a HooBuy holiday shopping timeline with evidence gates, stop-adding dates, warehouse review, parcel decisions and a no-guarantee arrival buffer.
hoobuy-holiday-shopping-timeline-spreads.body:
A HooBuy holiday shopping timeline cannot be built from one advertised transit estimate. The order passes through separate stages: product verification, purchase, seller movement, warehouse arrival, evidence review, possible correction, parcel preparation, international transport and local delivery. Delay at any stage can consume the buffer reserved for the next.

The practical solution is a spreadsheet with evidence gates and stop dates. Instead of predicting an exact delivery day, the sheet identifies the latest date at which you will still add products, the conditions required to submit a parcel and the fallback when the timeline becomes too uncertain.

Start with the real need date

Record when the item is needed and why. A gift exchange, departure date and general seasonal use have different consequences. Add a fallback outcome: buy locally, give later, choose a non-date-sensitive gift or remove the item from the holiday parcel.

Do not use the event date as the target delivery day. Choose an earlier personal readiness date that leaves time to inspect the parcel and handle local delivery variation. The size of that buffer is a risk preference, not a platform guarantee.

Separate the timeline into controllable stages

Create one row per order item and one parcel summary. Track discovery complete, identity verified, ordered, seller movement observed, warehouse arrival, QC reviewed, issue resolved, parcel submitted, carrier acceptance and delivery. Use account labels exactly as they appear rather than inventing a universal status dictionary.

Each stage needs an observed date, evidence source, owner and next action. A planned date should never overwrite an actual timestamp. Keeping plan and observation separate exposes drift early.

StageEvidence gateFallback trigger
DiscoveryExact listing and selected variant verifiedArchive unresolved links
Seller movementCurrent account event or support evidenceReview alternatives and current options
WarehouseItem identity and required evidence reviewedDo not approve an unresolved mismatch
ParcelContents, weight, dimensions and route checkedRemove nonessential blockers
InternationalCarrier event and destination details recordedUse evidence-based escalation, not repeated guessing

Set a stop-adding date before shopping

The stop-adding date is the point after which no new product enters the holiday parcel. It prevents one late seller or unresolved variant from holding an otherwise ready group. Choose it by working backward from the personal readiness date and leaving space for every stage that still has uncertainty.

Do not publish a universal number of days. Product type, seller behavior, warehouse evidence needs, current route and destination all vary. Record the reasoning and update the decision if a stage consumes more buffer than planned.

Timeline rule: a new item added after the cutoff becomes a separate future parcel candidate. It does not silently reset the schedule for products already ready.

Finish product verification before the cutoff

Use the link verification workflow to save the final URL, marketplace, item and seller identifiers, selected option wording, price state and check date. A gift deadline is not a reason to accept an ambiguous variant.

Add a “decision complete” field. The item can move forward only when identity, intended option, sizing basis and important inclusion questions are resolved. If it remains uncertain at the cutoff, archive it or move it to a non-holiday list.

Give sizing its own evidence gate

For clothing or footwear, record the exact source chart and compare compatible measurements before ordering. Use the size-chart spreadsheet method rather than a generic label conversion. A rushed size guess can create an after-sale issue that the timeline cannot absorb.

Personalized or customized items need an additional confirmation gate for text, number, style and applicable current conditions. Do not assume they can be changed or returned after work begins.

Track seller movement item by item

Record the order identifier, purchase time, latest observed account event and the date on which you will reassess. Do not group all products under one “ordered” cell. One stalled item can be invisible when the parcel summary shows only an average status.

When expected movement does not occur, consult the current account and support options. The spreadsheet should preserve screenshots or messages privately where appropriate, but the public guide should not invent a fixed dispatch promise.

Prewrite the warehouse review

Before products arrive, list the evidence required for each: identity, color, size label, quantity, key measurements, visible condition, customization and included pieces. Separate must-have evidence from nice-to-have views so the review can happen promptly without becoming careless.

Use clear outcomes: approve, request targeted evidence, inspect current after-sale options or remove from the holiday parcel. A deadline does not change a mismatch into an acceptable item. It changes which fallback is realistic.

Protect a parcel-decision window

Do not let the planned submission date equal the final warehouse arrival date. Reserve time to review all items, resolve blockers, confirm address details, check packed data and compare currently available routes. Record who performs the final review and which fields must be complete.

Keep a parcel manifest with item IDs, quantities, selected options and approval dates. This connects product rows to the parcel and reduces confusion when several similar items are stored.

Use current packed data and route eligibility

Seller-stated weight can help early planning, but the parcel decision should use the best current warehouse and packing information available. Record actual or measured values separately from estimates, including dimensions and packaging choices.

Route availability and pricing can depend on destination, contents and packed parcel. Confirm live choices at submission. Do not lock the calendar to a line name or an old quote saved from another parcel.

Plan for customs and carrier handoffs

International movement can include carrier acceptance, origin transport, border processing, destination handoff and last-mile delivery. A pause in public tracking does not by itself identify the cause. Record the last confirmed event, timestamp and source before escalating.

Keep destination details accurate and preserve current parcel documents. This guide cannot provide customs or legal advice, and no spreadsheet eliminates inspection or operational delays. The timeline should accommodate uncertainty rather than hide it.

Define three decision points

At the first decision point, remove unresolved products before ordering. At the second, decide whether a late or disputed warehouse item should wait for a later parcel. At the third, submit only when the manifest, evidence and live route checks are complete.

Write the fallback beside each decision. A good holiday plan remains useful when the ideal path fails because the next action was chosen in advance, without pressure from a shrinking deadline.

Worked example: one late item should not hold four

A parcel plan contains two tops, shoes, a bag and a customized item. Four products reach the warehouse with required evidence. The customized item has no confirmed completion state and its details cannot be rechecked. The stop-adding date has passed and the parcel-decision window is closing.

The spreadsheet should not replace uncertainty with an optimistic arrival guess. Keep the four ready products in the current manifest if their live parcel checks pass. Move the unresolved product to a later decision and use its gift fallback. The holiday plan remains honest and actionable.

Holiday timeline checklist

  • Need date, personal readiness date and fallback are recorded.
  • Every stage has planned and actual dates in separate fields.
  • A stop-adding date is fixed before discovery expands.
  • Listing identity, variant and sizing gates are complete.
  • Seller movement is tracked per item.
  • Warehouse evidence requirements are written in advance.
  • A parcel-decision window remains after item arrival.
  • Estimated and measured weight are not mixed.
  • Live route and address checks occur before submission.
  • No row presents a guaranteed holiday delivery date.

Use the calendar to stop, not just to start

The central skill in holiday planning is ending discovery soon enough to protect later decisions. A longer product list is not progress if its newest item removes the time needed for verification, warehouse review and parcel submission.

Maintain the calendar inside the core HooBuy spreadsheet, preserve actual timestamps and archive anything that misses a gate. The result cannot guarantee arrival, but it can prevent avoidable late additions and make every fallback visible before the deadline becomes urgent.

hoobuy-product-link-verification-taobao-.title: HooBuy Product Link Verification: Taobao, 1688 and Weidian
hoobuy-product-link-verification-taobao-.description: Verify Taobao, 1688 and Weidian product links before saving them to a HooBuy spreadsheet, with checks for seller, variant, price, domestic freight and link drift.
hoobuy-product-link-verification-taobao-.body:
A product link is not verified merely because it opens. For a spreadsheet and product-discovery user, verification means that the URL still identifies the intended listing, seller and variant, and that the current information is detailed enough for a purchasing agent to act without guessing. Taobao, 1688 and Weidian links can remain technically live while the selected colour disappears, the seller changes a variant label, a price applies only to a minimum quantity, or the page begins showing a different item.

If you are still deciding what to search for, start with the keyword-search workflow for better product finds; this page begins after a candidate URL exists. The safest verification workflow preserves two things at once: the original marketplace source and a dated snapshot of the decision-critical facts. The source lets an agent reach the listing. The snapshot lets you notice link drift before paying. Neither replaces the live order screen, and neither proves seller reliability or product quality. It simply reduces avoidable ambiguity at the first handoff.

Start with identity, not price

Open the original marketplace page rather than a screenshot, shortened redirect or copied image. Record the marketplace, seller display name, item title, listing identifier where visible and the date checked. Then compare the main images and option labels with the product you intended to save. A similar title is not enough: duplicate listings can use the same photographs while offering different materials, size ranges or included parts.

Paste the source link into the live agent interface only after the source identity is clear. If it resolves to a product screen, compare the seller, title and selectable options again. A successful parse shows that the interface can read something from the URL; it does not establish that every option, promotion or quantity rule was transferred perfectly. When fields disagree, treat the source listing and the final checkout display as two records that need reconciliation, not as interchangeable pages.

Verification rule: a usable find answers “which seller, which listing, which exact option, how many units and what was shown today?” A URL that answers only “what kind of product?” belongs in a research list, not an order-ready sheet.

Use one row per buyable variant

A spreadsheet row should represent the configuration you might actually order. If the same listing has two colours or sizes under consideration, create separate rows or make the unresolved choice explicit. Do not write “black/grey, M/L” in one cell and expect a later buyer to remember the intended combination.

FieldWhat to recordWhy it matters
Source identityMarketplace, seller, listing ID or stable URL, check dateDistinguishes the source from copies and later replacements
Exact variantSource-language option, plain-English note, colour, size and quantityReduces selection guesses and translation drift
Live amountDisplayed item amount, quantity basis, domestic freight if shownSeparates a headline price from the order-ready amount
Evidence limitsMissing chart, unclear material, preorder, custom item or no-return warningKeeps unresolved risk visible instead of hiding it in a link
Next checkOrder-ready, seller question, compare alternative or rejectGives the row a purpose

Keep the original-language variant text even when you add an English explanation. Translation is helpful for browsing, but the original label is what can be compared with the seller's page and the agent order. If the listing uses image-only options, write a positional cue and a distinguishing description rather than relying on “option 3.” Positions can change.

Taobao: watch option-specific changes

For a Taobao find, check whether the displayed amount changes after selecting the intended colour and size. Record the selected combination, not the page's lowest visible headline amount. Verify whether the size chart belongs to that exact listing and whether the seller identifies measurements or only generic labels. A product photo, title and size code together form the identity; none should be treated as conclusive alone.

If a previously saved link now opens another listing or a removed page, retain the old source in an archive field and mark it dead. Search for a replacement as a new candidate rather than silently replacing the URL in the same row. That preserves the evidence behind earlier price and QC records. A replacement seller is a new find, even if the photographs look identical.

1688: verify quantity and variant basis

On 1688, the amount shown may depend on quantity or a mix of variants. Before calling a row order-ready, confirm the number of units represented by the current selection and whether the desired combination can be purchased at that quantity. Do not infer a minimum order or wholesale tier from an old spreadsheet note. Recheck the live listing and the order screen because those conditions can change.

When several variants share a tier, record the planned quantity per variant as well as the total. “Three units” is incomplete if the seller requires a particular combination. If a pack, set or component count is unclear, flag it for a seller question. A low unit amount is not useful when you do not know what one unit contains.

Weidian: preserve seller and item references

For a Weidian find, save both the item link and the seller identity visible at the time of checking. Compare the option names and any visible seller notices with your planned order. Short social-media descriptions often omit variant or return conditions, so they should not become the source record. The marketplace listing is still the decision point.

Links shared through redirects or tracking parameters should be opened and resolved before saving. Keep a clean working URL when possible, but do not remove characters unless you have confirmed the result reaches the same seller and item. “Link cleanup” should remove unnecessary wrappers, not rewrite the product identity.

Run a five-minute pre-payment recheck

  1. Open the saved source and confirm it still identifies the same marketplace, seller and product.
  2. Select the intended variant again; compare the source-language option with the sheet.
  3. Check the current item amount, quantity basis and any domestic freight shown. Do not reuse a historical figure.
  4. Paste the original source into the current agent interface and compare the parsed seller, title, options and amount.
  5. Read visible warnings for availability, preorder, customization or return limitations. If unclear, pause the row.
  6. Save the agent order ID after purchase without deleting the marketplace URL.

This recheck is deliberately close to payment. A spreadsheet can organize product discovery, but it cannot freeze inventory, seller terms or a live amount. Add a “last checked” date and let stale rows expire from the order-ready view. You can keep them in an archive for research and link recovery.

Score readiness without pretending to score quality

A simple traffic-light label is enough. Green means the source, seller, variant, quantity basis and current order display agree. Amber means the item is identifiable but one decision field needs confirmation. Red means the link is dead, changed, contradictory or too incomplete for an unambiguous order. This score measures record readiness, not authenticity, seller honesty or manufacturing quality.

After purchase, stop editing the original row as if it were still a browsing candidate. Attach the agent order ID and preserve the ordered variant. Warehouse QC is a later evidence layer. Compare visible arrivals with the frozen purchase record using the W2C and QC workflow. The existing spreadsheet method shows how to extend the row with QC and shipping decisions without losing the source trail.

What product-link verification can and cannot prove

Verification can show that you saved a current, actionable listing and described the requested option accurately. It can expose a price basis that changes with quantity, a missing size, a seller switch or a dead link. It cannot prove that stock is physically available, that the seller will dispatch on a certain date, or that the received item will match expectations. Those require later seller, carrier and warehouse evidence.

A high-quality product-discovery sheet therefore contains fewer “mystery links” and more explicit decisions. Keep the original source, write the exact variant, date variable facts and separate unresolved questions. When a link changes, create a new candidate instead of rewriting history. That discipline makes comparisons fairer, purchasing instructions clearer and later QC disputes easier to explain.

Evidence ledger and limits

  • S1 — HooBuy Help Center. Checked August 12, 2026. Confirms that the public support structure includes shopping-agent guidance, payment, delivery, warehouse, inspection, returns and refunds.
  • S2 — HooBuy, “About Us.” Checked August 12, 2026. Supports only HooBuy's statement that it offers purchasing, quality checks, storage and shipping services.
  • S3 — Current HooBuy public product interface. Checked August 12, 2026. Product routes require a source link or product parameters; pages without sufficient parameters do not establish a buyable item.

Official sources describe HooBuy's own service categories and interface. The marketplace-specific verification fields, readiness labels, archival rule and examples are independent editorial analysis. No seller reliability, stock, price, domestic freight, minimum quantity, return right, fee, dispatch time or outcome is asserted for an unidentified product.

hoobuy-keyword-search-better-product-fin.title: HooBuy Keyword Search for Better Product Finds
hoobuy-keyword-search-better-product-fin.description: Build better HooBuy product finds with a keyword-search workflow for category, material, feature, size and seller terms, then verify every source link before ordering.
hoobuy-keyword-search-better-product-fin.body:
Better product discovery begins before you paste a link into an agent. A useful keyword search translates a vague idea—“heavy grey hoodie,” “small leather shoulder bag,” or “running shoe with a wide toe box”—into attributes that a marketplace listing can actually express. The goal is not to produce the longest result page. It is to find a small set of candidates whose identity, option and current terms can be verified.

This matters for spreadsheet users because weak queries create weak records. A generic brand or category phrase often returns unrelated styles, sponsored placements, unavailable variants and copies of the same seller images. If those links are saved without an intent note, the spreadsheet becomes a memory test. A structured query keeps the reason for each candidate visible and gives you a fair basis for comparing it later.

Write a search brief before writing a query

Start with the intended use, not a product nickname. Describe the category, must-have attributes, acceptable alternatives and deal-breakers. For clothing, useful fields may include garment type, intended fit, fabric or construction term, colour family and measurable sizing evidence. For bags, record shape, approximate dimensions, closure, strap type and hardware requirements. For shoes, separate intended use, silhouette, material, closure and available size evidence.

A search brief should also state what you do not know. If material is uncertain, mark it as a question instead of inserting a confident term. If two shapes are acceptable, keep them as separate query branches. This prevents search results from quietly changing the original intent.

Example brief: “Zip hoodie for cool-weather layering; relaxed fit; dark neutral colour; visible size chart with chest width; avoid cropped cuts; exact fabric composition still unknown.” This brief can produce several testable queries without pretending that a listing photo proves weight, warmth or composition.

Build queries from five keyword layers

LayerExamplesWhat it controls
Core categoryzip hoodie, shoulder bag, low-top shoeKeeps results in the right product family
Construction or materialdouble zip, canvas, knit, rubber soleSeparates visibly different builds; still requires listing verification
Shape or fitboxy, relaxed, mini, wide, croppedNarrows silhouette and sizing intent
Featureinside pocket, removable strap, embroidered graphicTargets a decision-critical detail
Variant or audiencecolour family, size range, adult, unisexFilters candidates that cannot offer the needed option

Begin with the core category plus one high-value attribute. Add another layer only when the results are too broad. A query containing every desired characteristic can fail because sellers use different words, omit details from titles or place them in images. Search is an exploration stage; verification happens on the product page.

Create a query ladder instead of one “perfect” phrase

A query ladder tests intent from broad to specific. The first rung identifies the category. The second adds the attribute most likely to remove irrelevant results. The third adds a second distinguishing feature. The fourth can test a synonym or source-language term. Save the query beside the candidates it produced so you can understand why the link entered the sheet.

For the hoodie brief, a ladder might move from “zip hoodie” to “relaxed zip hoodie,” then “relaxed double-zip hoodie,” and finally a source-language equivalent. Do not combine results from every rung into one unranked list. Keep a shortlist from each branch and compare whether the added term improved relevance or merely reduced variety.

Use neutral category language first. Starting with hype terms such as “best,” “1:1” or “premium” does not create evidence; it selects listings that use those marketing labels. Search for observable attributes, then inspect the source page.

Translate concepts, then verify marketplace wording

Machine translation can help generate source-language keywords, but it should not be treated as a product specification. A translated term may describe a different construction, fit or cultural category. Test it, then read how candidate listings use the word alongside measurements, option names and images. Keep both the English intent and the original source-language term in your notes.

When a result page repeatedly uses an unfamiliar term, do not immediately adopt it as fact. Open several listings and ask what attribute the term appears to distinguish. If the meaning remains unclear, retain it as a discovery label and flag the actual feature for verification. The spreadsheet should never turn a translation guess into a material claim.

Compare candidates by evidence, not result position

Search position can change and does not prove seller quality. For each candidate, capture the seller identity, listing URL, current title, selected variant availability, amount basis, domestic freight if shown, size or dimension evidence, and the date checked. A candidate that answers the important questions can be more useful than a visually appealing result with missing terms.

Candidate testKeep whenReject or pause when
IdentitySeller, item and intended category remain clearThe page redirects, changes item or depends on a screenshot
VariantNeeded colour, size and quantity can be selectedThe intended option is absent or ambiguous
EvidenceMeasurements, included parts and visible features can be checkedDecision-critical details appear only in unsupported claims
TermsCurrent amount basis and visible warnings are recordedA historical spreadsheet price is the only cost evidence

Do not compare two candidates as if they are equivalent merely because the main image matches. They may have different option sets, sellers, quantity rules, materials or included parts. Write the difference that justifies keeping both. If you cannot name it, one may be a duplicate research record.

Use negative filters in your notes, not unsupported search tricks

Marketplace search syntax varies, so do not assume that a minus sign, quotation mark or English operator works consistently. Instead, use your brief as a manual negative filter. Mark deal-breakers such as no measurements, preorder only, unclear set contents, unavailable size or a customization condition you cannot satisfy. Review candidates against that list before promoting them to “order ready.”

This approach is slower than trusting a search operator, but it is transparent. Anyone reviewing the sheet can see why a listing was excluded, and a rejected link can be reconsidered if its evidence changes.

Turn a promising result into an order-ready record

  1. Open the original marketplace listing, not only an agent preview or social post.
  2. Record the seller, stable source URL or listing identifier, and check date.
  3. Select the exact colour, size, model and quantity you may buy.
  4. Compare the current amount, quantity basis and domestic freight shown.
  5. Capture the measurement chart or dimension evidence that applies to that listing.
  6. Write one unresolved question and one category-specific QC focus.
  7. Paste the original source into the current agent interface and compare what was parsed.
  8. Classify the row as research, needs confirmation, order ready or rejected.

The companion product-link verification guide covers the source, seller and variant checks for Taobao, 1688 and Weidian. The spreadsheet method explains how to preserve the original query and candidate history after purchase.

Refresh saved searches without erasing history

A useful spreadsheet has a “last checked” date and a reason to recheck. Refresh a candidate before payment, when a chosen variant disappears, when the seller changes the listing, or when the recorded evidence is old enough that it no longer supports the decision. Archive the previous state rather than replacing it silently.

If a source link dies, return to the search brief and query ladder. Do not search only by the old listing title, because that title may contain seller-specific noise. Use the core category and the attributes that mattered. A replacement is a new candidate with a new seller and evidence record, even when the photos resemble the old find.

What keyword search can and cannot do

Keyword search can make product discovery more deliberate. It can reveal alternate terminology, eliminate incompatible variants and document why one candidate was shortlisted. It cannot prove stock, seller reliability, product authenticity, material performance, fit, dispatch speed or warehouse outcome. Those claims require their own evidence and later handoffs.

The result of a good search is not a giant collection of links. It is a smaller set of traceable candidates connected to a written intent. Build the query in layers, retain source-language wording, compare listings by the same fields and verify again before payment. That process turns product discovery from random browsing into a repeatable decision workflow.

Evidence ledger and limits

  • S1 — HooBuy Help Center. Checked August 14, 2026. Confirms that HooBuy publicly organizes shopping-agent guidance alongside payment, delivery, warehouse, inspection, returns and refunds.
  • S2 — HooBuy About Us. Checked August 14, 2026. Supports only HooBuy's own statement that purchasing, quality checks, storage and shipping are offered.
  • S3 — Current HooBuy public product interface. Checked August 14, 2026. Pages require sufficient source or product parameters; a page that opens without usable product information is not an order-ready source.

Official sources establish HooBuy's stated workflow, not the quality of a marketplace listing. The search brief, keyword layers, query ladder, candidate tests and refresh rules are independent editorial analysis. No ranking position, search volume, seller performance, price, fee, stock, return right or product quality is claimed.

hoobuy-1688-finds-moq-variants-seller-qu.title: HooBuy 1688 Finds: MOQ, Variants and Seller Questions
hoobuy-1688-finds-moq-variants-seller-qu.description: Compare HooBuy 1688 finds by minimum order, price tier, exact variant, domestic freight, seller evidence and questions that must be resolved before purchase.
hoobuy-1688-finds-moq-variants-seller-qu.body:
Finding a low displayed price on 1688 is not the same as finding a buyable option. A listing may show a price tied to a quantity tier, a color-size combination may have its own availability, domestic delivery may appear later, and a supplier image may cover several products that are not included together. A useful HooBuy 1688 finds spreadsheet must record the purchase basis, not just the headline amount.

This guide focuses on the decision that comes after discovery: which 1688 candidate can be specified clearly enough for a purchasing agent to order and later verify? The goal is not to predict seller quality. It is to reduce ambiguity about minimum quantity, price tier, variant, included pieces and unresolved questions before money moves.

Start with the final source page

Open the exact 1688 source URL and save it before comparing anything. Remove tracking fragments only if the product identity remains unchanged. Record the supplier or shop name shown, listing title, product or offer identifier and date checked. If HooBuy resolves the link, compare the imported title and options with the source instead of assuming the import is complete.

Use the existing product-link verification workflow when identity is uncertain. This article begins after the source has been linked correctly. It does not repeat dead-link recovery or generic W2C cleaning.

Record MOQ as a rule, not a single number

MOQ means the minimum quantity required for the relevant purchase. The important phrase is “for the relevant purchase.” A supplier may show different conditions by option, assortment or quantity band. Your sheet should never contain only “MOQ: 2” without explaining whether two identical pieces, two mixed colors or two units across selected variants satisfy the live listing.

FieldWhat to captureDo not assume
Minimum quantityDisplayed threshold and its scopeDifferent variants can always be mixed
Tier priceQuantity band tied to the unit amountThe lowest unit price applies to one piece
Selected quantityTotal pieces and pieces per optionThe cart will automatically correct the plan
Package basisPiece, pair, set, pack or other stated unitOne listing unit equals one physical item

If the requirement is unclear, mark “question open.” Do not choose a convenient interpretation. HooBuy's beginner guide says shopping agents can contact sellers during purchasing and may ask the buyer for missing information. Turn that handoff into a precise question rather than an instruction to “please check everything.”

Match the price to the exact quantity tier

Create one row per candidate purchase scenario. Suppose a page displays unit price p1 for band q1, p2 for band q2 and p3 for band q3. If your intended quantity belongs to q1, the subtotal is intended quantity multiplied by p1, not by the more attractive p3.

Keep variables until the live page supplies values. Then record currency, tier, quantity, product subtotal and any domestic seller delivery amount shown during the current order. Do not mix the later international parcel estimate into the 1688 listing price. A supplier comparison becomes misleading when one row includes domestic freight and another silently omits it.

Spreadsheet rule: every price needs a basis: exact option, purchasing unit, quantity tier, currency and check date. A number without those fields is not comparable.

Expand variants into unambiguous order lines

Supplier pages can compress many colors, sizes, materials or models into one gallery. Your spreadsheet should expand them. Create a separate order line for each intended option and copy the exact label shown. Add an English note for your own use, but preserve the original label so the purchasing agent has a direct match.

For clothing, record color label, size label, quantity and seller measurement reference. For shoes, record model, colorway, size system and quantity. For hardware or accessories, capture dimensions, finish, connector or included-piece option. Never use the gallery's first image as proof of the selected variant.

HooBuy currently says it can capture information for most products from supported source marketplaces, not every product. If a variant field is missing or distorted after import, do not force the closest visible option. Save the source label and use an order remark or enquiry only where the live workflow offers it.

Ask seller questions that produce a decision

A good question identifies the offer, intended option and evidence needed. “Is this available?” is weaker than “For offer ID [recorded], can two units be ordered as one black size M and one grey size L under the displayed minimum?” The second question can confirm or reject a specific plan.

  • Can the displayed minimum be met by mixing the exact listed variants?
  • Which unit does the quoted price cover: piece, pair, set or pack?
  • Does the selected option include every item visible in the reference image?
  • Is the current variant ready to dispatch or produced after order?
  • Which seller measurement chart applies to the selected option?
  • Is domestic delivery shown for this quantity and warehouse destination?
  • Are custom notes required, and do they change return eligibility?

Do not bundle all questions into a long message if only one uncertainty blocks purchase. Ask the smallest decision-changing question first. Save the answer date and wording; do not promote an old reply into a permanent promise for later orders.

Separate supplier evidence from quality conclusions

A detailed listing can make a product easier to specify, but it does not guarantee received quality. Use seller-page fields as purchasing evidence: the exact option, material claim, dimensions, package contents and dispatch statement. Then use warehouse QC as later visual evidence about the delivered item.

HooBuy's beginner guide says items are inspected and photographed after warehouse arrival and specifically notes that 1688 purchases use a different quality-control standard. Because the public guide does not define a universal photo entitlement or acceptance threshold, write your own decision-critical QC notes before purchase. Examples include exact color, number of pieces, visible model marking, size label and one measurable dimension.

Compare candidates with a completeness score

Score each candidate on five binary fields: verified source identity, clear MOQ rule, matching price tier, unambiguous variant and answered critical question. A candidate with five confirmed fields is easier to order than one with a lower headline price but three unresolved fields.

This is not a seller rating. It measures whether your intended purchase can be described and audited. Keep quality claims, customer reviews and sales signals in separate columns with their own sources. Do not allow a popularity indicator to fill an evidence gap about the exact SKU.

Use a controlled comparison example

Imagine Candidate A shows a lower unit price at a higher quantity tier, while Candidate B has a higher unit price but a clearly buyable single-option quantity. Your need is two pieces in different colors. First check whether A permits mixed variants within the displayed minimum. If not confirmed, calculate A only for a compliant quantity or mark it unresolved. Do not multiply two pieces by the lowest displayed tier.

For each valid scenario, add product subtotal and current domestic delivery if shown. Record the number of unwanted extra units, if any. Then compare option clarity, seller answer and planned QC fields. The cheapest compliant scenario may differ from the cheapest number visible at the top of the page.

Pre-payment 1688 finds checklist

  1. Open and save the exact final source URL.
  2. Match source and imported product identity.
  3. Record the purchasing unit and minimum quantity rule.
  4. Select the quantity tier that actually covers the order.
  5. Expand every intended variant into its own line.
  6. Record current domestic seller delivery separately.
  7. Resolve the one question that could stop the purchase.
  8. Write visible QC priorities before submitting.
  9. Review the final live options, remarks, quantities and payable amount.

A useful 1688 find is orderable, not merely attractive

The best HooBuy 1688 finds record connects four things: the source offer, the valid quantity basis, the exact variants and a dated answer to any decision-critical question. That structure prevents a low tier price, broad gallery or ambiguous package unit from becoming a false promise in the spreadsheet.

Once a candidate is complete, preserve the row through purchase and warehouse receipt. Update it with the actual ordered quantities and QC result rather than overwriting the earlier plan. Product discovery then becomes a traceable workflow, not a collection of links whose meaning disappears when the listing changes.

Evidence ledger and limits

  • S1 — HooBuy Beginner's Guide. Checked August 28, 2026. Supports pasting or searching 1688 items, selecting available color, size and quantity, paying product and domestic delivery, contacting shopping agents and later warehouse inspection.
  • S2 — HooBuy public interface. Checked August 28, 2026. Supports product-link or name search and identifies 1688 among its source-marketplace workflows.
  • S3 — HooBuy Registration Agreement. Checked August 28, 2026. Describes assistance with designated products from 1688 sellers and limits guarantees about third-party seller information and goods.

Official sources establish the stated purchasing workflow, not any seller's current MOQ, price, dispatch or quality. The field schema, completeness score, questions and symbolic example are editorial methods. No seller performance, universal order capture rate, fixed QC entitlement or successful outcome is claimed.

hoobuy-spreadsheet-guide.title: HooBuy Spreadsheet 2026: Product Links, QC & Shipping
hoobuy-spreadsheet-guide.description: Build a HooBuy spreadsheet with verified product links, exact variants, size evidence, QC status, packed data and clear parcel decisions.
hoobuy-spreadsheet-guide.body:
A useful HooBuy spreadsheet is a decision record, not a page of product links. Every row should identify one exact listing and intended variant, show when its evidence was checked, preserve unresolved questions and connect later warehouse information to the same product.

This structure is designed for searches such as HooBuy spreadsheet, HooBuy finds and HooBuy product links. It helps an editor compare candidates without presenting a stale price, borrowed photo or seller claim as permanent fact.

Choose the unit of one row

Use one row for one source listing plus one intended option combination. If the page contains two sizes, colorways or constructions under active consideration, give them separate rows. This keeps the selected-state price, chart and later QC evidence attached to the correct choice.

Assign a stable candidate ID before writing a nickname. The ID survives translated titles, seller edits and internal reorganization. When a destination or seller changes, create a new version instead of silently rewriting the old evidence.

BlockCore fieldsPurpose
SourceMarketplace, final URL, item ID, seller IDReproduces the listing identity
SelectionOriginal option labels, quantity, intended useDefines the exact order target
EvidenceChart, claims, images, check date, unknownsSeparates facts from assumptions
WarehouseOrder ID, item ID, QC state, measurementsConnects received evidence
ParcelWeight, dimensions, restrictions, decisionSupports current shipping checks

Verify every product link before saving it

Open the shared link, record the original URL and save the final destination after any redirect or translation layer. Capture the marketplace, item identifier, seller or shop identifier and verification date. A matching image alone does not prove that two links lead to the same product.

Use the complete Taobao, 1688 and Weidian link checklist when an address is shortened, dead or redirected. Mark unresolved identity as a blocker; do not move it into the ready list.

Preserve exact option wording

Record every selected color, size, version, bundle and customization label in its original wording. Place translations and editorial explanations in separate fields. This makes the choice reproducible and prevents a familiar nickname from replacing the source option.

Save the displayed price only after selecting the intended combination. Keep amount, currency, quantity, domestic freight state and observation time separate. A headline minimum may belong to another variant and should not be presented as the cost of the intended item.

Design evidence fields by category

Generic columns are not enough. Shoes need size-system, foot-length, label, outsole and packaging fields. Hoodies need chest, length, sleeve method, fabric claim, print and stated weight. Jerseys need edition, customization, spelling and badge fields. Bags need exterior dimensions, hardware and included pieces.

Link category rows to the shoes, hoodie, jersey or bags spreadsheet method. Shared identity fields remain stable while category evidence changes.

Record size evidence without universal conversions

Keep source labels, original measurements, units, endpoints, measurement type and tolerance notes. Compare a candidate only with a reference garment or foot measurement taken on a compatible path. Do not assume that a familiar letter or number has the same dimensions across listings.

The size-chart workflow explains how to separate flat width from circumference, garment length from body measurement and foot length from insole or outsole length. Missing method data should remain visible.

Separate seller claims from observations

Create one field for what the seller states and another for what a current image or warehouse record visibly shows. Material, performance, durability, authenticity and comfort cannot be confirmed from appearance alone. Attribute every claim and date it.

Add an evidence-type field: selected listing text, general page text, image only, seller response, warehouse photo or measured warehouse value. This prevents a broad statement from being applied to an option it may not describe.

Spreadsheet rule: never replace an unknown with a guess. An empty or blocked field is useful because it identifies the next action.

Write QC questions before ordering

Plan only the views or measurements that could change the decision. Start with product identity, selected color, size and quantity. Then add category-specific checks such as visible condition, construction, print placement, hardware, included pieces or defined measurement endpoints.

Keep expected evidence and received evidence in separate columns. Use statuses such as pending, matched, mismatch, unclear, missing or not applicable. A warehouse photo can show the specific item and captured surface; it cannot prove hidden composition or long-term performance.

Connect order and warehouse identifiers

After ordering, append the platform order identifier and later warehouse item identifier to the original candidate. Do not start a disconnected row that loses the source evidence. Preserve selected options and order notes exactly as submitted.

When an account event changes, add a timestamped update rather than rewriting the earlier state. The sequence is important when diagnosing a wrong option, seller delay or missing evidence. Use live labels from the account instead of inventing a universal status list.

Keep product amount and parcel planning separate

Product cost, domestic freight, optional services and international parcel charges occur at different stages. Give each its own block. Seller-stated weight belongs in an estimate field, while warehouse-measured weight and packed dimensions belong in later evidence fields.

Do not calculate a permanent shipping price from an old quote. Destination, contents, restrictions, packaging, actual weight, volumetric treatment and current routes can change. Record the current checkout decision and its date without presenting it as a universal rate.

Use statuses that drive action

  1. Discovered: link saved but identity is incomplete.
  2. Verified: listing, seller and intended option can be reproduced.
  3. Blocked: a sizing, inclusion, restriction or evidence question remains.
  4. Ready: critical fields are complete for the current decision.
  5. Ordered: order identity is linked to the row.
  6. QC review: warehouse evidence is being assessed.
  7. Parcel ready: approval and current shipping checks are complete.
  8. Archived: completed, rejected, dead or replaced, with a reason.

A numerical score may help sorting, but it must not override a blocker. One missing critical measurement can matter more than several strong listing images. The action status should remain explicit.

Maintain freshness without deleting history

Use separate fields for last listing verification, row edit, order event, QC review and parcel decision. When a seller changes the title, price or variants, append the new observation. Keep the version that informed an existing order.

Schedule rechecks for rows that remain in discovery. Dead or changed links should move to an archive with a reason. The seller-page checklist helps determine whether a replacement deserves a new record.

Use seasonal deadlines as stop rules

A spreadsheet can also control when discovery ends. For a seasonal shortlist, define the real use case and cap the number of overlapping products. For deadline-sensitive purchases, set a stop-adding date and move late candidates to a future parcel.

See the autumn finds shortlist and holiday timeline for practical examples. Neither framework promises delivery; both prevent one late or weak item from holding everything else.

Minimum HooBuy spreadsheet checklist

  • One stable row ID per exact listing and intended variant.
  • Original and final links with marketplace, item and seller identity.
  • Complete original option labels and selected-state price.
  • Category-specific size, construction and inclusion fields.
  • Seller claims attributed and separated from observations.
  • Blocking unknowns and next actions kept visible.
  • Order and warehouse identifiers linked to the source row.
  • Expected and received QC evidence stored separately.
  • Estimated, measured and packed values labeled by stage.
  • Dated status history and archive reason preserved.

Make every row explain the next decision

The best HooBuy spreadsheet is not necessarily the largest. It is the one another editor can audit: the exact listing is reproducible, the intended option is clear, the evidence source is labeled and uncertainty has not been disguised as certainty.

Start with a small set of verified candidates and add category fields only when they support a decision. Preserve history, recheck live details and let blockers stop the workflow. That structure turns product links into a maintainable research system from discovery through parcel planning.

hoobuy-weidian-finds-options-seller-sign.title: HooBuy Weidian Finds: Options and Seller Signals
hoobuy-weidian-finds-options-seller-sign.description: Organize HooBuy Weidian finds by source item, exact option, seller-page evidence, price basis and unresolved questions before adding a product to your spreadsheet.
hoobuy-weidian-finds-options-seller-sign.body:
Useful HooBuy Weidian finds are not just rows of product links. Each row should preserve one source item, one intended option and the seller-page evidence visible on the date of research. That distinction matters because a page can remain live while its options, price basis, seller identity or description changes.

The goal is not to predict whether a seller is “good.” It is to create a reproducible record: another person should be able to open the row, identify the same item and option, see what was known before ordering, and understand which questions still require confirmation.

Start with the item, not the shop reputation

A promising shop cannot rescue an ambiguous item record. Save the canonical Weidian item URL, item identifier if exposed, page title, selected image reference and research date before collecting broader seller signals. If a shared link contains tracking or temporary parameters, keep a clean source URL while storing the original shared URL in a separate provenance field.

Then open the page through the current HooBuy purchasing workflow and confirm that the destination record refers to the same source item. If the parser displays incomplete choices or different data, mark the row “manual confirmation required.” Do not silently substitute a similar listing.

Row rule: one row represents one source item plus one intended option. Different sellers, batches or materially different options deserve separate rows even when the photos look alike.

Capture the exact option grammar

Weidian option labels can encode color, size, version, batch, package or another seller-defined distinction. Copy the visible labels exactly before adding an English note. Do not shorten “black / upgraded version / size 42” to “black 42,” because the omitted version may change the product and price.

Spreadsheet fieldRecordDo not infer
Source optionExact visible label in original orderThat two similar labels are equivalent
Plain-language noteYour separate interpretationThat the translation replaces the source text
Displayed priceAmount tied to the selected state and dateThat every option has that price
QuantityIntended unitsThat pictured bundles are included
Unresolved questionOne answer needed before purchaseA favorable answer

If a price changes only after selecting an option, save the selected state. If no option can be selected in the available view, treat the displayed amount as a page-level observation, not a confirmed SKU price.

Separate seller signals into three evidence levels

Level 1: source identity

Record the shop name or identifier displayed on the item page and the seller-page URL when available. This supports attribution. It does not prove that a similarly named shop is the same entity.

Level 2: current listing evidence

Record the description, option set, price state, disclosed domestic freight and visible policy text relevant to the selected item. These are transaction inputs, not general reputation scores.

Level 3: historical interface signals

A shop page may expose counts, dates, badges or other historical indicators. Preserve the label and value only if its meaning is clear in the interface. If the method, time window or denominator is not explained, store it as “uninterpreted signal” or omit it. Never turn it into a quality percentage.

This hierarchy prevents weak signals from outweighing strong item evidence. A polished storefront, large catalog or visible count cannot confirm the fabric, batch, measurements or condition of the selected unit.

Build a Weidian discovery row

  1. Paste the clean source item URL and save the shared-link provenance separately.
  2. Record the source item ID, title and seller identifier where visible.
  3. Copy every option label needed to reconstruct the intended SKU.
  4. Select the intended state and save its displayed price and date.
  5. Record domestic freight only when it is shown for the relevant state.
  6. Save the seller description claims as claims, not verified facts.
  7. Write one blocking question for every ambiguous option or inclusion.
  8. Set the row status: research, ready to order, ordered, warehouse review or rejected.

The existing HooBuy spreadsheet guide provides the broader status model. For Weidian finds, add three dedicated columns: source option text, seller-signal evidence and unresolved question.

Use rejection rules before collecting more links

Reject a find when the source item cannot be identified, the required option is absent, the price basis cannot be connected to a selectable state, or a critical inclusion is ambiguous and cannot be confirmed. More attractive photos do not repair these gaps.

Also reject a row that merges two sellers because one has better images and the other has a better price. That creates a synthetic listing that neither seller offered. Compare the rows side by side instead.

Compare candidates without inventing equivalence

DimensionCandidate ACandidate B
Source identityItem and seller IDs recordedSeller ID missing
Option matchExact size/version selectableSimilar wording only
Price basisSelected-state price savedHeadline amount only
MeasurementsRelevant chart tied to itemGeneric chart
Open questionPackaging inclusionVersion identity and packaging

Candidate A has a stronger record, but the table still does not prove superior quality. It shows fewer evidence gaps for the exact intended option. That is the correct product-discovery conclusion.

Write seller questions that can change the order

A useful question names the source item and option, asks one factual point and states the required evidence. Examples include: “Does this selected version include the accessory pictured in image four?” or “Please confirm whether the measurement chart belongs to this exact option.” Avoid “Is it good quality?” because the answer has no shared test.

Store the question, answer, date and channel together. If no answer arrives, preserve the missing evidence. Silence is not confirmation. If an answer conflicts with the page, keep both records and ask which one controls the order.

Move from discovery to warehouse review

When ordering, copy the intended source option into the order note without rewriting it. After warehouse arrival, match the order record, item identity and visible option before evaluating condition. HooBuy's current beginner guide supports inspection after arrival, but it does not make source claims true automatically.

Use QC to check observable details: visible color option, label, included parts, print placement or other item-specific evidence. Do not expect photos to prove material composition, hidden construction, durability or authenticity. Link the resulting decision back to the original find rather than overwriting pre-order evidence.

Dead links and changed pages need version history

If the source link dies, retain the last verified date, item ID, seller ID, option text and saved reference. Search for a replacement as a new candidate. Never reuse the old row while changing only its URL; that erases the provenance of the original find.

If the page remains live but options or price change, add a new observation date. The product-link verification guide explains the general identity check. This article's narrower task is preserving the Weidian option and seller evidence that makes the row actionable.

Common Weidian spreadsheet mistakes

  • Saving only a short or redirected link.
  • Using a shop name without an item identifier.
  • Translating option text and deleting the original.
  • Recording the lowest displayed amount as every option's price.
  • Treating catalog size, badges or unexplained counts as quality proof.
  • Merging images, descriptions and prices from different sellers.
  • Marking an unanswered seller question as resolved.
  • Overwriting the source row after warehouse QC.

A strong find is reproducible

HooBuy Weidian finds become useful when the spreadsheet can reconstruct the selected source item without relying on memory. Preserve identity first, then exact option grammar, selected price state, seller-page evidence and unresolved questions. Rank evidence gaps instead of sellers.

This method will not guarantee stock, dispatch, quality or after-sale eligibility. It produces something more defensible: a dated research record that shows why a candidate was ready to order, why another was rejected, and what warehouse evidence must be checked next.

hoobuy-org-w2c-spreadsheet-method-2026.title: Hoobuy W2C Spreadsheet Method: Fields & QC Status
hoobuy-org-w2c-spreadsheet-method-2026.description: Organize Hoobuy W2C sources, selected variants, link checks, QC status, follow-up evidence, parcel notes and final decisions in one spreadsheet.
hoobuy-org-w2c-spreadsheet-method-2026.body:
Treat every spreadsheet row as a dated research record. Confirm current product details, services, fees and parcel options on the live destination before acting.

A page full of product cards can help discovery, but a bare link does not explain what was checked or whether the listing later changed. A more useful Hoobuy spreadsheet connects each W2C source with the selected variant, verification date, QC evidence and parcel decision.

FieldsW2C sourceQC statusNotesDecision

1. Use fields that support a decision

Recommended fields include product name, category, source marketplace, seller, exact URL, selected colour and size, date checked, link status, price basis, domestic freight note, QC status, follow-up evidence, packed weight, route note and final decision.

2. Document the W2C source

A W2C cell should do more than hold a URL. Record why the candidate was saved, which seller and option were reviewed, and what could make the record invalid. If the source is unclear, later QC comparison becomes unreliable.

3. Use clear QC states

Useful states include waiting for warehouse arrival, evidence ready, review needed, follow-up requested, approved, held and return considered. This prevents completed and unresolved items from being mixed together.

4. Write decision-changing notes

For shoes, note size labels, outsole, heel shape and pair symmetry. For clothing, note measurements, collar, stitching and print placement. For bags and accessories, note hardware, zippers, dimensions and included pieces. Avoid vague notes such as “looks good.”

5. Record the final action and reason

Before parcel submission, review unresolved evidence, packed weight, dimensions, route eligibility, protection and the live final amount. Record the action—approve, hold, request evidence, return or remove—with a short reason and date.

Summary

A maintainable Hoobuy spreadsheet turns scattered links into a repeatable verification workflow. Clear fields make it easier to spot stale listings, unresolved QC questions and parcel risks before they become avoidable mistakes.

hoobuy-seller-page-checklist-before-savi.title: HooBuy Seller-Page Checklist: Verify Before Saving a Find
hoobuy-seller-page-checklist-before-savi.description: Use this HooBuy seller-page checklist to verify listing identity, exact options, price evidence, dispatch clues and unresolved risks before saving a product find.
hoobuy-seller-page-checklist-before-savi.body:
A useful product spreadsheet begins one step before the product row: with a decision about whether the seller page is clear enough to save at all. The common failure is collecting a visually attractive link first and trying to repair its missing identity, option and price evidence later. By then, a redirected URL or edited page may make the original find impossible to reconstruct.

This HooBuy seller-page checklist is a pre-save gate. It works across Taobao, 1688 and Weidian without pretending that their page fields mean the same thing. The result is one of three statuses: save, save with a blocking question, or reject. That is more useful than a vague seller score.

Gate 1: prove which page you are saving

Open the final destination rather than recording only a shared, shortened or redirected address. Save the clean source URL, source marketplace, visible item identifier and seller or shop identifier where available. Keep the original shared link in a separate provenance field if it helps explain where the find came from.

Compare the page title, main image context and seller identity with the record shown in the current purchasing flow. A parser can omit details or show stale information. If the destination changes to a search page, shop homepage, login wall or different item, stop. A similar product is a new candidate, not a repaired version of the old one.

Identity test: another editor should be able to open the saved row and reach the same source item without relying on your screenshot, memory or translated nickname.

Gate 2: connect the intended option to the displayed amount

Record the exact source-language labels for every choice needed to reconstruct the intended SKU. Color, size, version, package and batch can be separate selectors. Add a plain-language note in another column, but never replace the original labels with the note.

Then select the intended combination and observe whether the displayed amount changes. Save the amount, currency, selected state and date together. A headline price, range minimum or promotional banner does not prove the price of your chosen option. If an option cannot be selected, mark the price unconfirmed rather than copying the lowest visible number.

FieldMinimum evidenceStop condition
Item identityFinal URL plus visible item ID or equivalentRedirect resolves to another item or generic page
Seller identityShop name or identifier tied to the itemSeller cannot be attributed
Intended optionComplete original labels in selection orderRequired version or size is absent
Price basisAmount observed after selecting the intended stateOnly a range minimum or unrelated option is visible
Observation dateDate the live page was checkedRow relies on an undated copied value

Gate 3: separate product claims from observable facts

A seller may describe material, construction, measurements, included parts or performance. Preserve important claims as attributed page text. Do not rewrite them as verified facts. Images may support visible design details, but they cannot prove hidden construction, fiber composition, durability or authenticity.

Measurement evidence is stronger when the chart is clearly tied to the exact listing and option. A generic shop chart or image copied between products deserves an uncertainty flag. For apparel, record which points are measured and the unit. For shoes or bags, record whether dimensions describe the product, insole, packaging or an unspecified reference.

Gate 4: capture transaction-specific seller evidence

Seller-page signals are most useful when they change this transaction. Record visible domestic freight, preorder wording, customization terms, disclosed dispatch notes, return restrictions and option-specific inclusions. Keep each field dated and quote only the short label needed to identify its meaning.

Badges, sales counts, follower totals and shop age can be context, but only when the interface explains them. Do not convert an unexplained number into a defect rate or reliability percentage. A popular shop can still have an ambiguous listing; a smaller shop can have a well-documented item. The row should rank evidence completeness, not social proof.

Use a two-column claim log

In the first column, record what the page states. In the second, record what would confirm it: a selectable option, seller answer, warehouse label, measurement image or included-part photo. This prevents a claim from silently becoming a spreadsheet fact while keeping the question actionable.

Gate 5: write one blocking question

A blocking question is a fact whose answer could change the order. It names the exact item and option, asks one thing, and describes acceptable evidence. “Is the blue large option the same version shown in image six?” is actionable. “Is the quality good?” is not.

Save the question before marking the row ready. If an answer arrives, record the answer, date and channel beside the original page evidence. If it conflicts with the listing, keep both records and ask which one will control fulfillment. No reply means unresolved, not approved.

Apply a save, hold or reject decision

DecisionUse whenNext action
SaveIdentity, intended option and price basis are reproducible; no material ambiguity remainsAdd the row with its verification date
HoldIdentity is clear but one inclusion, measurement, dispatch term or option distinction is unresolvedSave as research only and attach the blocking question
RejectThe destination, seller, intended option or amount cannot be connected reliablyRetain a brief rejection reason; search for a new candidate

Do not let a low price override a reject result. An unidentifiable item has no defensible comparison basis. Do not let a polished storefront override a hold result either. The question belongs to this exact transaction.

Worked example: two similar hoodie pages

Candidate A has a final item URL, shop identifier, selectable charcoal / size L / standard version, a price that updates for that state, a listing-specific measurement chart and a dated dispatch note. Candidate B has stronger photos and a lower headline amount, but its version label is missing and the chart appears generic.

Candidate A can be saved if its measurements meet the requirement. Candidate B stays on hold until the seller confirms which version the amount covers and whether the chart belongs to it. The conclusion is not that A has better quality. It is that A has a more reproducible pre-order record.

Transfer the record without flattening it

When a find is ready, move the exact option labels and blocking requirements into the order note. Preserve the discovery row as a dated snapshot. The product-link verification guide covers link identity across marketplaces, while the spreadsheet guide provides the broader status workflow.

After warehouse arrival, compare the received item with the order record. QC can confirm observable identity, selected color, visible label, measurements shown in requested evidence and included parts. It should not overwrite what the seller page claimed or be treated as proof of hidden material and long-term performance.

Recheck whenever the page state matters

Reopen the source page before ordering, after a long hold, and whenever price or option data changes. Add a new observation rather than replacing the earlier one. If the URL dies, retain the item and seller identifiers, last verified state and rejection or recovery note. A replacement belongs in a new row.

  • Final destination and item identity verified.
  • Seller identity attributed to this item.
  • Original option labels preserved in full.
  • Selected-state price and date recorded.
  • Claims kept separate from observable evidence.
  • Domestic freight and special terms recorded only when displayed.
  • Unexplained badges or counts left uninterpreted.
  • One blocking question written where needed.
  • Save, hold or reject status assigned with a reason.

The best saved find has fewer hidden assumptions

A seller-page checklist cannot guarantee stock, dispatch, quality or returns. It can prevent an attractive but ambiguous page from becoming a false spreadsheet fact. Verify identity, reconstruct the exact option, tie the amount to that state, preserve dated claims and make unresolved questions visible.

That discipline makes later comparisons fair. It also gives the purchasing and warehouse stages a precise target. Save the find only when someone else can understand what you intended, what the page actually showed and what still needs proof.

Complete parcel workflow

Shipping and QC FAQ

Product routes

Parcel checklist
